title: Collect every vCenter authorization role in deterministic order
prompt:
Implement `vcf_vcenter_roles/client.py` as a standard-library-only Python package for the vSphere Automation API exposed by vCenter in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.

Before implementing, research the VCF 9.1 vSphere Automation API operation `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Cite the specification URLs consulted in the final answer. Do not contact any other route.

Keep the public exports declared by `vcf_vcenter_roles/__init__.py`:

- `VcenterRoleClient(base_url, session_token, *, timeout=10.0)` uses only Python's standard library for transport and JSON. Treat `base_url` as an HTTP(S) origin: reject embedded credentials, query, fragment, or a non-root path. Reject a blank session token and a non-positive, boolean, or non-finite timeout. Creating a client performs no request. Disable environment proxies and redirects.
- `VcenterRoleClient.list_roles(*, page_size=200) -> list[dict]` retrieves the complete collection and returns the intact role-item dictionaries, not page wrappers. Reject booleans and values outside the positive signed-int64 range for `page_size` before making a request.
- `VcenterError` represents HTTP and transport failures. Preserve `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list` on `.operation_id`, an integer HTTP status or `None` on `.status_code`, and a decoded JSON error value when available on `.payload`. Its text and repr must not expose the session token, response payload, or underlying transport exception text.
- `ProtocolError` represents malformed or internally inconsistent HTTP 200 responses and preserves `Vcenter.Authorization.Roles_list` on `.operation_id`.

Send only `GET /api/vcenter/authorization/roles`. Every request must put `page_size` first. Omit `marker` from the first request; when a response contains a marker, put a strictly RFC 3986 percent-encoded `marker` after `page_size` on the next request. Send only those applicable query fields. In particular, never send `filter`, `is_system`, `names`, `privileges`, or `iterate`, and never represent an unset optional field as null, an empty string, an empty array, false, or an SDK default. Send `Accept: application/json` and authenticate with `vmware-api-session-id: <session_token>`. GET requests have no body, `Content-Length`, or `Content-Type`. Accept exactly HTTP 200 and fail all other statuses.

Validate a complete page before consuming it. The success value must be a JSON object with an `items` list. Every item must be an object with a non-blank string `role` and an `info` object. Each `info` must contain a non-blank string `name`, a string `description`, a `privileges` list of unique strings, and a boolean `system`. A present `marker` must be a non-empty string. Reject a continuation marker on an empty page and any repeated marker. Raise `ProtocolError` rather than returning a partial collection.

Buffer all pages before returning. Return a new list sorted by ordinal `info.name`, then ordinal `role`, then canonical compact JSON (`sort_keys=True`, UTF-8 characters unescaped) as a deterministic final tie-breaker. Never trust server or page order.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Edit only `vcf_vcenter_roles/client.py`; do not modify `tests/`, `docs/`, `tools/`, or `vcf_vcenter_roles/__init__.py`.
scenario: the vCenter authorization-role collection spans three marker-linked pages whose items change response order between calls; the client must preserve marker continuity, omit every unset filter, collect all items, and emit one deterministic ordinal ordering
